reconcile.connective: Commentators resolve the count by inclusive reckoning: counting Adam as the first link, Enoch is genuinely the seventh in Seth's line.

discrepancy.connective: The objection comes from Steve Wells's Skeptics Annotated Bible, which lists the count as a contradiction yet concedes in its own note that Jude is quoting the Book of Enoch, not the Genesis genealogy.

skeptic.name: Steve Wells
skeptic.attribution: Steve Wells, The Skeptics Annotated Bible (2013), "Was Enoch the sixth or the seventh from Adam?"

excerpts.excerpt_text: In Enoch, the seventh from Adam through Seth, godliness attained its highest point …
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Directly answers the sixth-vs-seventh question: Keil & Delitzsch affirm Enoch is 'the seventh from Adam through Seth,' the inclusive count (Adam=1) that matches Jude 14 against the Genesis list.

pd_work.resource: Keil & Delitzsch, Biblical Commentary on the Old Testament (1861-75), on Genesis 5
pd_work.author: Keil & Delitzsch
pd_work.note: Keil & Delitzsch treat this passage directly, identifying Enoch as 'the seventh from Adam through Seth' and linking the title to Jude 1:14-15.
